answer.summary: No explicit memory retrieval mechanisms under contextual perturbations are reported in Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1, necessitating a bounded minimal operational definition for retrieval-based memory integrity as a fallback anchor.
answer.content: After two review cycles, the absence of explicit mechanisms for memory retrieval under contextual perturbations remains unchallenged. A minimal operational definition of retrieval-based memory integrity is proposed, anchored in latency and recall performance under defined perturbation conditions (e.g., session interruption), but this lacks direct source validation. The current evidence does not support claims of superior memory management without such bounded criteria. A different, more targeted research question is now required to advance the inquiry meaningfully without overreaching the available data.
